item.content:encoded:
The First Gen Fellowship 2026 is offering financial support to first-generation college students in the United States who are experiencing significant financial hardship while pursuing undergraduate or graduate education.

In 2026, the First Gen Fund will award 50 fellowships worth $1,000 each, providing a total of $50,000 in direct financial hardship relief to selected first-generation students.

The funding is intended to help students manage educational expenses and essential costs connected to their studies, including fees, books, housing, basic needs, professional development activities and opportunities, and transportation related to school.

Applications opened on September 2, 2026, and must be submitted by September 16, 2026. The application portal states a closing time of 9:00 PM Eastern Time (ET), while the main fellowship page states 6:00 PM Pacific Time (PT). These times correspond to the same deadline, so applicants should ensure that their application is fully submitted before the stated closing time rather than waiting until the final minutes.

Awardees will be contacted directly and announced on National First-Gen Day, November 8, 2026, through the First Gen Fund’s Instagram account and its website.

What Is the First Gen Fellowship 2026?

The First Gen Fellowship is designed to provide direct financial assistance to first-generation college students who are facing financial hardship.

Unlike opportunities that primarily fund research, tuition-only scholarships or institutional projects, this fellowship is specifically intended to provide financial hardship relief to individual students. The grant can be used for a broad range of education-related expenses, allowing recipients to address costs that may otherwise interfere with their ability to continue their studies.

The 2026 program will select:

  • 50 first-generation students
  • $1,000 for each selected fellow
  • $50,000 in total fellowship funding

The program recognizes that students may experience financial challenges for a variety of reasons, including limited family financial support and unexpected expenses.

Applicants are therefore given more than one way to demonstrate financial hardship.

First Gen Fellowship 2026 Grant Amount

Each selected recipient will receive a $1,000 grant.

The program describes these awards as providing financial hardship relief directly to first-generation students.

The $1,000 funding can be particularly useful for students who are dealing with education-related expenses that may not be fully covered by existing financial aid.

Applicants should understand that the fellowship is not simply based on being a first-generation student. To qualify, applicants must meet all of the program’s eligibility requirements, including enrollment status, age, academic standing, first-generation status and financial hardship.

What Can the First Gen Fellowship Grant Be Used For?

Recipients must use their fellowship funds for educational expenses.

The program provides several examples of eligible expenses, including:

  • College and university fees.
  • Books and other educational materials.
  • Housing.
  • Basic needs.
  • Professional development opportunities and activities.
  • Transportation related to school.
  • Other expenses connected to education.

This flexibility allows students to use the grant where the financial need is most relevant to their educational journey.

For example, a student could potentially use the funding to address the cost of required academic materials, transportation to and from school, housing-related expenses or professional development activities that support their education.

Applicants should ensure that their intended use of the funds is connected to their education and falls within the program’s permitted expenses.

Who Is Eligible for the First Gen Fellowship 2026?

The First Gen Fellowship has specific eligibility requirements, and applicants must satisfy all of the stated criteria.

1. Applicants Must Be Full-Time Students

Applicants must currently be enrolled as full-time students in either:

  • An undergraduate program; or
  • A graduate program.

The institution must be an accredited college or university in the United States.

This requirement means the fellowship is intended for students who are actively pursuing higher education rather than individuals who have already completed their studies.

Important international student restriction

The eligibility guidelines explicitly state that funding is limited to domestic students.

International applicants are not eligible.

Therefore, students who are studying at a U.S. college or university but are classified as international students should not assume that enrollment in the United States makes them eligible.

The program’s eligibility information specifically limits this funding to domestic students.

2. Applicants Must Identify as First-Generation College Students

Applicants must identify as first-generation college students.

The First Gen Fund acknowledges that family backgrounds can be complex and encourages applicants to identify with the definition of first-generation status that most accurately reflects their lived experience.

This means that applicants should consider their own family and educational circumstances when determining whether they identify as first generation.

Because the fellowship is specifically designed for first-generation students, this is a fundamental requirement of the program.

3. Applicants Must Be in Good Academic Standing

Applicants must be in good academic standing with their college or university.

The program generally defines good academic standing as:

  • Meeting the institution’s minimum GPA requirements; and
  • Not being on academic probation for any reason.

Students who are uncertain about their academic standing are encouraged to confirm their status with their registrar or academic advisor before completing the application.

This requirement is important because applicants should not assume that being enrolled automatically means they meet the academic-standing requirement.

4. Applicants Must Be at Least 18 Years Old

Applicants must be 18 years of age or older at the time of application.

This means an applicant who has not yet reached their 18th birthday when submitting the application does not meet the stated age requirement.

5. Applicants Must Demonstrate Significant Financial Hardship

Financial need is one of the central requirements of the First Gen Fellowship.

Applicants must demonstrate significant financial hardship through one or both of the following routes:

Pell Grant or other need-based aid

Applicants may demonstrate financial hardship by showing that they are eligible for a Pell Grant or other need-based financial aid.

This provides one way of establishing that the applicant has significant financial need.

Personal statement explaining financial hardship

Applicants may also explain their financial circumstances through a personal statement.

Examples of financial hardship mentioned by the program include:

  • Lack of parental financial contribution.
  • Unexpected expenses.
  • Other circumstances that create significant financial difficulty.

Applicants should use the personal statement to clearly and honestly explain how their financial circumstances affect their education and why the fellowship support would be meaningful.

6. Fellowship Funds Must Be Used for Educational Expenses

The fellowship is intended to support students’ education.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed use of the $1,000 grant relates directly to their educational needs.

Eligible examples include:

  • Fees.
  • Books.
  • Housing.
  • Basic needs.
  • Professional development opportunities and activities.
  • Transportation related to school.
  • Other education-related expenses.

The funding should not be viewed as unrestricted personal income. Recipients are expected to use the award for eligible educational expenses.

How to Apply for the First Gen Fellowship 2026

The First Gen Fund provides an online application process that consists of several stages.

Applicants should carefully complete each stage and ensure that their application is ultimately submitted as a final application before the deadline.

Step 1: Register

Applicants must first click the Register option and complete and submit the registration form.

Registration creates the applicant’s account for accessing the fellowship application system.

Step 2: Log In

After registering, applicants can log in to the award platform using their email address and password.

Applicants should keep their login details secure and accessible throughout the application period.

Step 3: Create the Application

Once logged in, applicants can begin creating their online fellowship application.

Applicants should carefully provide the requested information and ensure that their responses accurately reflect their academic, first-generation and financial circumstances.

Step 4: Save the Application as a Draft

During the application period, applicants can save their application as a DRAFT while they continue completing the required sections and uploading attachments.

The system indicates when individual application sections have been completed. Applicants should take advantage of this functionality rather than trying to complete the entire application in one sitting.

Saving the application as a draft also gives applicants an opportunity to review their responses and supporting materials before submission.

Step 5: Submit the Final Application

After completing all required sections and uploading the necessary attachments, applicants must save the application as FINAL.

Simply registering an account or saving an application as a draft does not constitute final submission.

Applicants should therefore confirm that their application has been submitted as a final application before the deadline.

APPLY HERE

First Gen Fellowship 2026 Application Deadline

The application period for the 2026 First Gen Fellowship is short.

Key dates

  • Applications open: September 2, 2026, at 12:00 PM ET
  • Applications close: September 16, 2026, at 9:00 PM ET
  • Deadline equivalent: September 16, 2026, at 6:00 PM PT
  • Award announcement: November 8, 2026, on National First-Gen Day

The main fellowship page states the deadline as September 16 at 6:00 PM Pacific Time, while the application portal lists September 16 at 9:00 PM Eastern Time. These represent the same point in time.

Applicants should submit well before the deadline to avoid technical difficulties or incomplete applications.

Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

When Will First Gen Fellowship Winners Be Announced?

Selected awardees will be contacted directly by the First Gen Fund.

The recipients will also be announced on National First-Gen Day on November 8, 2026.

The announcement will be made through:

  • The First Gen Fund’s Instagram account, @firstgenfund; and
  • The First Gen Fund website.

Applicants should therefore monitor the official channels around the announcement date.

What Makes This Fellowship Important?

First-generation college students can face financial challenges that affect their ability to participate fully in higher education.

Expenses such as books, transportation, housing, basic needs, university fees and professional development can accumulate alongside tuition and other educational costs.

The First Gen Fellowship is designed to provide direct assistance to students experiencing these challenges.

The $1,000 grant can help reduce immediate financial pressure and enable recipients to continue focusing on their education.

The fellowship also recognizes that financial hardship is not always captured entirely by traditional financial-aid systems. By allowing applicants to demonstrate hardship through a personal statement, the program provides an additional avenue for students whose circumstances may include limited parental support or unexpected expenses.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Because the application period is limited and the program receives a high volume of applications, applicants should prepare carefully.

Confirm your eligibility first

Before starting the application, make sure you meet every requirement:

  • You are at least 18 years old.
  • You are a full-time undergraduate or graduate student.
  • You attend an accredited U.S. college or university.
  • You are a domestic student.
  • You identify as a first-generation college student.
  • You are in good academic standing.
  • You can demonstrate significant financial hardship.
  • You will use the funding for eligible educational expenses.

Prepare your financial hardship explanation

If using a personal statement to demonstrate financial hardship, applicants should provide an honest and clear explanation of their circumstances.

Rather than simply saying that money is needed, applicants should explain the nature of the financial challenge and how it affects their educational experience.

Identify eligible expenses

Applicants should have a clear understanding of how the $1,000 fellowship would support their education.

Consider which eligible expense would provide the greatest immediate benefit to your academic journey.

Do not wait until the final day

The application system allows applicants to save their work as a draft. Use this feature to complete the application gradually and review everything before final submission.

Late applications will not be considered.

High Volume of Applications and Individual Eligibility Questions

The First Gen Fund states that it receives a high volume of applications.

To ensure an impartial review process, the organization explains that it is unable to respond to correspondence regarding individual applications.

The same applies to questions about individual eligibility.

Applicants should therefore carefully review the published eligibility criteria before applying and use the information provided by the First Gen Fund to determine whether they meet the requirements.

First Gen Fellowship 2026 at a Glance

Feature Details
Opportunity First Gen Fellowship 2026
Organization First Gen Fund
Number of awards 50
Award amount $1,000 per recipient
Total funding $50,000

Study level Undergraduate and graduate
Enrollment Full-time

Minimum age 18 years

Winner announcement November 8, 2026

Visit HERE to learn more about the First Gen Fellowship 2026.

Conclusion

The First Gen Fellowship 2026 is a valuable funding opportunity for first-generation undergraduate and graduate students in the United States who are experiencing significant financial hardship.

With 50 grants of $1,000 each, the fellowship provides direct financial support that recipients can use for eligible education-related expenses, including fees, books, housing, basic needs, professional development and school-related transportation.

However, applicants must meet all eligibility requirements. They must be at least 18 years old, full-time students enrolled in an accredited U.S. college or university, identify as first-generation college students, remain in good academic standing, and demonstrate significant financial hardship. The program’s guidelines also make clear that eligibility is limited to domestic students, meaning international applicants are not eligible.

The application period runs from September 2 to September 16, 2026, giving prospective applicants only a limited amount of time to prepare and submit their applications. Since late applications will not be considered, eligible students should begin the process early, prepare their financial hardship information carefully, complete all required sections and attachments, and ensure that the application is saved as FINAL before the deadline.

Awardees will be contacted directly and publicly announced on November 8, 2026, National First-Gen Day.

For first-generation students facing financial barriers while pursuing higher education, this fellowship can provide meaningful short-term financial relief while helping them remain focused on their academic and professional goals.

item.content:encoded:
The EY Foundation is accepting applications for a Policy and Research Officer, offering an exciting permanent career opportunity for professionals with experience in research, policy development, stakeholder engagement, project management and evidence-based decision-making.

Based in London, Birmingham, Manchester or Glasgow, the position will join the EY Foundation’s Influence Team and contribute directly to the organisation’s work to improve employment opportunities and outcomes for young people from low-income backgrounds.

The EY Foundation is expanding the capacity of its influence function, and the newly recruited Policy and Research Officer will play an important role in supporting this growth. The successful candidate will provide research and policy expertise, strengthen the evidence base underpinning the Foundation’s activities, and contribute to its external policy and public affairs voice.

This is a hands-on and delivery-focused position particularly suited to someone who is confident working across research and policy and who can translate evidence and complex information into practical insights and actions.

Application Deadline: 20 September 2026

About the EY Foundation

The EY Foundation is a charity established in 2014 with the purpose of helping young people from low-income backgrounds develop the skills they need to succeed in the workplace.

The organisation was founded by EY, the professional services firm, which continues to serve as its primary funder.

The Foundation’s ambition is for young people who are eligible for Free School Meals to have employment and earnings potential that is equitable with that of other young people across the United Kingdom.

Its approach is informed by an understanding of both sides of the labour market. By bringing together young people and employers, the Foundation seeks to address barriers to employment while helping young people develop skills and access opportunities.

Its activities include:

  • Delivering employability skills programmes.
  • Developing scalable digital interventions.
  • Collaborating with a wide range of organisations.
  • Bringing employers and young people together.
  • Using its convening power to influence systemic change.
  • Building evidence that can support improvements in employment and skills outcomes.

The EY Foundation operates across regions of the UK, with team members based in four main hubs: London, Manchester, Glasgow and Birmingham.

As an independent charity, it raises income through corporate partnerships, traditional fundraising activities and grants.

Where Will the Policy and Research Officer Be Based?

Applicants may be based in one of four locations:

  • London
  • Birmingham
  • Manchester
  • Glasgow

The EY Foundation operates a hybrid working model.

Staff ordinarily work from the office for at least one day each week. However, depending on the responsibilities associated with the position and specific organisational requirements, employees may occasionally be expected to attend an office or external events more frequently.

Candidates should therefore consider their ability to work effectively within this hybrid arrangement when applying.

About the EY Foundation Policy and Research Officer Role

The Policy and Research Officer will become part of the EY Foundation’s Influence Team and report to the Policy and Public Affairs Manager.

The position is national in scope and is closely connected to the Foundation’s ambition of helping young people from low-income backgrounds access meaningful employment opportunities.

The successful candidate will contribute to the implementation of the Foundation’s influence strategy by designing and coordinating impactful research projects and ensuring that research is robust, relevant and informed by the lived experiences of the young people the organisation supports.

The Policy and Research Officer will also help shape the Foundation’s policy agenda.

This will include producing policy briefings, responding to consultations and developing relationships with relevant external stakeholders with the aim of influencing change at a systemic level.

The Foundation describes the opportunity as particularly suitable for someone who thrives in a dynamic and purpose-led environment and is passionate about using evidence to advance equity and opportunity.

A strong commitment to social mobility, diversity and inclusion is also expected.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities associated with the EY Foundation Policy and Research Officer position span research, project management, policy development and stakeholder engagement.

1. Conduct Research and Landscape Reviews

The successful candidate will undertake comprehensive landscape reviews.

These reviews will help identify gaps in existing evidence and research and inform the development of future projects.

This requires the ability to assess substantial amounts of information, identify meaningful trends and gaps, and translate findings into useful recommendations.

2. Maintain a PESTLE Analysis

The Policy and Research Officer will maintain and update a quarterly PESTLE analysis.

PESTLE covers:

  • Political factors
  • Economic factors
  • Social factors
  • Technological factors
  • Legal factors
  • Environmental factors

This analysis will be used to inform the Foundation’s research priorities, policy positioning and approach to stakeholder engagement.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable analysing external developments and understanding how wider political, economic and social changes may affect the organisation’s priorities and the young people it supports.

3. Develop Research Briefs

Another important responsibility will involve developing research briefs and invitations to tender.

The successful candidate will advise on suitable research methodologies and approaches, requiring a sound understanding of both qualitative and quantitative research.

Research Project Management

Project management forms a significant component of the position.

The successful candidate will lead the delivery of internal and external research projects and ensure that projects:

  • Are delivered within agreed timelines.
  • Remain within their defined scope.
  • Align with the EY Foundation’s strategic objectives.
  • Produce robust and useful outputs.

This means applicants should be comfortable taking ownership of research initiatives from initiation through to completion with relatively limited supervision.

The Policy and Research Officer will also plan and deliver stakeholder engagement events. These activities will provide opportunities to gather insights from stakeholders and communicate research findings.

The successful candidate will work with the communications team to support effective dissemination of research and insights.

Policy Development and Stakeholder Engagement

The position goes beyond conducting research. A major part of the role involves translating evidence into policy engagement and influence.

Policy Briefings

The successful candidate will produce timely briefings responding to:

  • Policy developments.
  • New research reports.
  • Relevant sector trends.
  • Other developments affecting the Foundation’s areas of interest.

These materials will be developed for both internal and external audiences.

Consultation Responses and Policy Submissions

The Policy and Research Officer will draft consultation responses and policy submissions.

These submissions must align with the Foundation’s priority areas while accurately reflecting its established policy positions and wider public affairs strategy.

Briefing Materials and Presentations

Candidates will prepare briefing materials and presentations for a variety of important engagements, including:

  • Meetings
  • Conferences
  • High-profile events
  • Stakeholder discussions

The ability to communicate complicated research findings and policy issues clearly and persuasively will therefore be particularly important.

Stakeholder Relationships

The successful candidate will identify and engage relevant stakeholders who can help disseminate research findings and advance the Foundation’s influence.

Stakeholders may include policymakers, researchers, funders and other organisations working within relevant sectors.

Engagement activities and follow-up actions will also need to be recorded through the Foundation’s CRM system. This will help maintain accountability and enable the organisation to assess the impact of its stakeholder relationships.

Required Skills

Applicants should demonstrate strong capabilities across research, analysis, communication, project management and stakeholder engagement.

The required skills include:

Advanced Analytical Skills

Applicants should demonstrate expertise in advanced analytical methodologies.

Candidates need a proven ability to interpret and synthesise complex data drawn from multiple sources and use this information to inform strategic decision-making.

Exceptional Written Communication

Strong written communication is essential.

Applicants should have demonstrated experience producing high-impact materials such as:

  • Research reports.
  • Strategic briefings.
  • Policy documents.
  • Evidence-based materials designed to influence stakeholders.

The successful candidate must be able to transform complicated research and evidence into clear, persuasive and actionable communications.

Project Management

Candidates need strong project management capabilities and should be comfortable overseeing the different stages of research projects from initiation through to completion.

They should be able to operate with minimal supervision while ensuring projects remain aligned with wider strategic objectives.

Organisation and Attention to Detail

Strong organisational skills and careful attention to detail are required.

The successful candidate will need to coordinate multiple activities while maintaining high standards across research, policy and stakeholder-facing outputs.

Stakeholder Engagement

Applicants should have demonstrated experience developing strategic relationships with a range of external stakeholders.

These could include:

  • Policymakers
  • Researchers
  • Funders
  • Sector organisations
  • Other relevant external partners

Relationship-building is important because these connections can strengthen the organisation’s credibility and expand its ability to influence change.

Knowledge Requirements

Candidates are expected to bring extensive professional or technical knowledge and experience within their specialist area.

They should have a comprehensive understanding of:

  • Qualitative research methodologies.
  • Quantitative research methodologies.
  • Ethical research practices.
  • Policy issues relating to young people.
  • Education policy.
  • Skills and employment.
  • Stakeholder mapping and engagement.
  • Policy and public affairs environments.

Importantly, candidates should have thorough knowledge of the policy landscape in England and Scotland, particularly in relation to young people, education, skills and employment.

Applicants should also understand the challenges and barriers experienced by young people who are eligible for Free School Meals or who come from low-income backgrounds.

The successful candidate should understand how to develop and deliver effective stakeholder mapping and engagement strategies within a policy or public affairs environment.

Professional Experience Required

Applicants should demonstrate relevant professional experience across research, evaluation, policy and stakeholder engagement.

The EY Foundation specifically seeks candidates with:

  • Proven experience coordinating or delivering research and evaluation projects.
  • Extensive experience using evidence to influence policy, programme design and organisational strategy.
  • Experience coordinating external-facing events, briefings and consultations.
  • Experience facilitating meaningful stakeholder engagement.
  • Experience presenting research findings to internal and external audiences.
  • The ability to communicate complex information clearly and persuasively.
  • Experience working with or within think tanks, charities and research consultancies.

These requirements indicate that the opportunity is aimed at applicants who can combine research expertise with practical experience applying evidence within policy, programme and organisational contexts.

Educational Qualifications

Applicants should hold a:

Degree or equivalent experience in a relevant discipline.

Examples of relevant disciplines provided by the EY Foundation include:

  • Social sciences
  • Education
  • Economics
  • Public policy
  • Research

Equivalent professional experience may also be considered, meaning the requirement is not limited exclusively to applicants following a particular academic pathway.

Desirable Skills and Experience

In addition to the required criteria, several skills and qualifications are considered desirable.

Data Analysis and Visualisation

Experience in data visualisation or statistical analysis would be advantageous.

Relevant tools may include:

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Power BI
  • SPSS
  • R

Applicants who can use these tools to analyse information and communicate research findings may bring additional value to the position.

Facilitation Skills

Experience facilitating workshops or gathering insights from young people and other stakeholders is desirable.

This could be particularly valuable when conducting participatory research or stakeholder engagement activities.

Participatory Research

Experience with participatory research methodologies, especially approaches involving young people, would strengthen an application.

Parliamentary and Public Affairs Knowledge

Knowledge of parliamentary processes and public affairs engagement strategies is another desirable attribute.

This would support the successful candidate in understanding how research and policy evidence can be used effectively within wider policy and decision-making environments.

Cross-Sector Partnerships

Experience supporting events or contributing to cross-sector partnerships is desirable.

Candidates may also benefit from experience working collaboratively across different organisational functions to translate programme insights into policy recommendations.

The Foundation values the ability to use research evidence not only to advocate externally but also to inform, refine and improve programme design and delivery internally.

Desirable Postgraduate Qualification

A postgraduate qualification in one of the following areas would be advantageous:

  • Research methods
  • Public policy
  • A related discipline

However, this is listed as desirable rather than as a mandatory requirement.

Recruitment and Interview Process

The EY Foundation uses a comprehensive recruitment process designed to assess applicants’ skills, motivation and potential.

Candidates progressing through the process should prepare for two interview stages.

First-Stage Interview

The first interview will assess candidates across three major areas.

Competency-based questions

Candidates will be assessed on technical and professional competencies relevant to the Policy and Research Officer position.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to provide clear examples demonstrating their research, policy, project management, analytical and stakeholder engagement capabilities.

Motivational questions

The interview will explore applicants’ motivations, passion for the work and alignment with the EY Foundation’s mission and organisational values.

Candidates should understand the Foundation’s purpose and be prepared to explain why they want to contribute to its work.

Scenario-based questions

Applicants will also respond to hypothetical scenarios.

These questions will provide candidates with an opportunity to demonstrate their:

  • Problem-solving skills.
  • Judgement.
  • Decision-making abilities.
  • Ability to respond to realistic professional situations.

Second-Stage Interview

Candidates progressing to the second stage will face additional assessments.

Presentation development

Candidates will be asked to develop and deliver a presentation on a topic connected with the position.

This will assess communication, presentation and potentially research and analytical capabilities.

Understanding of the organisation

Candidates will also be expected to demonstrate a strong understanding of the EY Foundation.

This includes knowledge of:

  • Its mission.
  • Its values.
  • The communities it serves.
  • The wider sector in which it operates.

Applicants who reach this stage should therefore undertake detailed preparation on the organisation and its work.

Important Recruitment Dates

Candidates should take note of the following dates:

  • Application deadline: 20 September 2026
  • First-round interviews: 1 and 2 October 2026
  • Second-round interviews: 7 and 8 October 2026

Applicants should consider their potential availability for these interview dates before submitting an application.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging at EY Foundation

Diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging form an important part of the EY Foundation’s organisational approach.

The Foundation states that it seeks to create an environment where people feel valued, respected and empowered to be themselves.

It is an Equal Opportunities Employer and welcomes applications from people representing different backgrounds, identities and experiences.

The organisation emphasises continuous learning and improvement as part of building an inclusive workplace in which individuals can thrive.

The successful Policy and Research Officer will also be expected to demonstrate a strong commitment to social mobility, diversity and inclusion.

Safeguarding Requirements

The EY Foundation is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.

Staff and volunteers are expected to share this commitment.

Successful candidates will need to undertake an Enhanced DBS check through the Disclosure and Barring Service where appropriate.

Applicants should be aware of this requirement before applying.

Accessibility During Recruitment

The EY Foundation states that it is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment experience.

Candidates requiring adjustments or additional support during recruitment, selection or onboarding are encouraged to communicate their requirements to the organisation.

This commitment extends across the recruitment and onboarding journey.

Why Consider the EY Foundation Policy and Research Officer Opportunity?

This position could be particularly attractive to research and policy professionals who want their work to contribute to wider social impact.

Rather than focusing exclusively on research production, the position connects several important areas:

  1. Research and evidence generation.
  2. Policy development.
  3. Public affairs.
  4. Stakeholder engagement.
  5. Project management.
  6. Youth employment and social mobility.
  7. Strategic organisational influence.

The successful candidate will have opportunities to turn evidence into practical policy and organisational action while contributing to the Foundation’s mission of improving opportunities for young people from low-income backgrounds.

It is therefore particularly relevant to professionals interested in the intersection of research, social mobility, youth policy, education, employment, public affairs and evidence-based policy development.

How to Apply for the EY Foundation Policy and Research Officer Position

Interested candidates should submit their application through the official EY careers recruitment platform.

Applicants should carefully review the complete position description and ensure that their application demonstrates how their qualifications, skills and professional experience align with the required criteria.

Given the nature of the role, candidates may particularly benefit from demonstrating concrete examples of:

  • Research projects they have led or coordinated.
  • Qualitative and quantitative research experience.
  • Research or evaluation methodologies they have used.
  • Policy documents or briefings they have produced.
  • How their research has informed policy or programme decisions.
  • Stakeholder relationships they have developed.
  • External events, consultations or briefings they have coordinated.
  • Examples of translating complex evidence into accessible recommendations.
  • Experience related to youth, education, skills, employment or social mobility.
  • Commitment to diversity, inclusion and equitable opportunities.

Candidates should also familiarise themselves thoroughly with the EY Foundation, its mission and its work before progressing to interview.

Application Deadline

Applications for the EY Foundation Policy and Research Officer position must be submitted by:

20 September 2026

Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare and submit their applications ahead of the closing date rather than waiting until the final day.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The EY Foundation Policy and Research Officer 2026 opportunity offers experienced research and policy professionals the chance to contribute to an organisation focused on improving employment prospects and economic opportunities for young people from low-income backgrounds.

As a permanent position based in London, Birmingham, Manchester or Glasgow, the role combines research, policy development, project management, stakeholder engagement and public affairs within a purpose-led environment.

The successful candidate will help develop the evidence underpinning the Foundation’s work, coordinate internal and external research projects, produce policy briefings and consultation responses, engage influential stakeholders and contribute to the organisation’s broader influence strategy.

Candidates with a relevant degree or equivalent experience, strong research capabilities, knowledge of qualitative and quantitative methodologies, policy expertise and experience translating evidence into action are particularly well aligned with the position.

With applications closing on 20 September 2026, interested candidates should review the requirements carefully, prepare evidence demonstrating their research and policy experience, and submit their application through the official EY recruitment platform before the deadline.

Visit the OFY website for more global Job Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026, an important higher education funding opportunity designed to support Pakistani women pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate education at Higher Education Commission (HEC)-recognised universities across Pakistan.

Funded by the Scottish Government and administered in Pakistan by the British Council, the scholarship programme aims to make quality higher education more accessible to women and girls, particularly those who may face financial, geographical, social or accessibility-related barriers to continuing their education.

The programme provides financial assistance towards tuition fees and other education-related expenses for eligible women studying selected priority subjects at universities in Pakistan. Depending on their level of study, successful applicants may receive support for a four-year bachelor’s degree or a master’s/MPhil programme lasting up to two years.

Women with disabilities, women from rural communities and women belonging to minority groups are particularly encouraged to apply.

Importantly, the application deadline has been extended to 15 September 2026, giving eligible candidates additional time to prepare and submit their applications.

About the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls programme is an initiative funded by the Scottish Government to increase access to higher education for Pakistani women.

Higher education can provide women with greater opportunities for professional development, economic participation, leadership and contribution to their communities. However, the financial costs associated with university education can prevent talented students from pursuing or completing their studies.

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships seek to address some of these barriers by providing financial support to eligible female students pursuing degrees in selected fields considered important for Pakistan’s social, economic and sustainable development.

The programme is administered by the British Council in Pakistan, which coordinates with successful scholars and their respective universities. Coordination may take place directly with scholarship recipients and universities or through nominated university focal persons.

What Levels of Study Are Supported?

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026 support eligible students at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels.

Applicants may be pursuing one of the following:

1. Four-Year Bachelor’s Degree

Female students pursuing a four-year bachelor’s degree at an HEC-recognised university in Pakistan may apply, provided their programme falls within one of the scholarship’s eligible subject areas.

This provides an important opportunity for young Pakistani women beginning or pursuing undergraduate higher education in fields connected to education, sustainability, agriculture, health, science, technology and climate.

2. Master’s or MPhil Degree

The programme also supports eligible women pursuing a master’s or MPhil degree of up to two years at an HEC-recognised university in Pakistan.

Applicants must be pursuing their postgraduate qualification within one of the programme’s designated subject areas and must meet all other eligibility requirements.

Financial Benefits of the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships 2026

Successful applicants can receive substantial financial support to help reduce the costs associated with pursuing higher education.

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls Scheme provides award holders with support that may include:

Tuition Fees

The scholarship covers tuition fees for courses in eligible subject areas.

Tuition costs can represent one of the largest financial barriers to university education. By providing support towards eligible tuition fees, the scholarship allows selected students to concentrate more fully on their studies and academic development.

University Hostel Costs

The scholarship provides support for university hostel costs where applicable.

This is particularly valuable for students who need to relocate from their home communities to attend university and require accommodation on or around their university campus.

Travel Between Home and University

Students staying in on-campus university hostels can receive support for travel between their home and university twice per year.

For students studying away from their families, particularly those coming from rural or geographically distant communities, this provision can help reduce the additional costs associated with university attendance.

Research Support for Master’s Students

Master’s-level scholarship recipients may also receive funding for research work to access quality laboratories, equipment and tools required for their chosen course of study.

This research support is specifically identified for master’s students and can be particularly valuable for candidates pursuing programmes requiring laboratory work, specialist equipment, practical research or technical resources.

Eligible Subject Areas

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026 are not available for every university discipline.

Applicants must be studying within one of the programme’s specified priority subject areas.

The scholarship covers eligible four-year bachelor’s degrees and up to two-year master’s degrees in the following areas:

Education

Students pursuing eligible programmes related to education can apply for scholarship support.

Education plays an important role in developing skilled communities, improving learning outcomes and strengthening future generations of educators and education professionals.

Sustainable Energy

Eligible programmes related to sustainable energy are covered by the scholarship.

As countries work towards more sustainable and resilient energy systems, expertise in renewable and sustainable energy is increasingly important for addressing environmental, economic and development challenges.

Food Security and Agriculture

Women pursuing eligible programmes related to food security and agriculture can also apply.

This area is particularly relevant to sustainable food production, agricultural development, rural livelihoods, food systems and long-term food security.

Health Sciences

The programme supports eligible students pursuing health sciences.

Supporting women in health-related education can contribute to strengthening healthcare capacity, research and services while creating additional professional opportunities for women in the sector.

STEM

Eligible programmes within Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) are included.

STEM education provides pathways into rapidly developing fields and can prepare women for careers in science, engineering, technology, research, innovation and related industries.

Climate

Eligible programmes related to climate are also supported.

With climate change creating increasingly significant environmental, social and economic challenges, developing expertise in climate-related disciplines can help prepare future professionals and researchers to contribute to climate resilience and sustainable development.

Who Can Apply for the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships 2026?

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls are specifically available to female applicants who satisfy the programme’s eligibility conditions.

Applicants must meet all of the following core requirements:

  • Be female.
  • Be a Pakistani national.
  • Be currently residing in Pakistan.
  • Be pursuing an eligible four-year bachelor’s degree or a two-year master’s degree.
  • Be studying within one of the scholarship’s approved subject areas.
  • Hold a confirmed admission offer from an HEC-recognised university in Pakistan.

Applicants should carefully review the relevant official scholarship FAQs before applying, particularly because separate guidance documents are available for bachelor’s and master’s applicants.

Encouragement for Women from Underrepresented Communities

One of the significant aspects of the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls is its emphasis on widening access to higher education.

The programme specifically encourages applications from:

  • Young women with disabilities
  • Women from rural areas
  • Women from minority groups

Candidates from these backgrounds who otherwise meet the scholarship criteria are therefore strongly encouraged to consider applying.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully review all official eligibility requirements and supporting documentation before submitting an application.

HEC-Recognised University Requirement

Applicants must hold a confirmed admission offer from an HEC-recognised university in Pakistan.

This is an important eligibility condition.

The scholarship is intended to fund eligible studies undertaken within Pakistan rather than study at a Scottish or other overseas university.

Applicants should therefore verify the recognition status of their university and ensure that their programme and admission status satisfy the scholarship requirements before submitting an application.

Is This Scholarship for Studying in Scotland?

Despite the programme being funded by the Scottish Government, the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls described in this call support eligible students pursuing their studies at HEC-recognised universities within Pakistan.

Applicants should not interpret the programme as a scholarship for travelling to Scotland or studying at a Scottish university.

The financial support is intended to improve access to higher education for Pakistani women studying in Pakistan.

How to Apply for the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships 2026

There are separate application links for bachelor’s and master’s candidates.

Applicants should use the application form corresponding to their level of study.

Bachelor’s Applicants

Candidates applying for scholarship support towards an eligible four-year bachelor’s degree can submit their application through the official bachelor’s application portal:

Apply here: https://www.research.net/r/WZQB3D5

Bachelor’s candidates should also consult the official document titled “Scotland Pakistan Scholarship FAQs and Bachelors 2026” available through the British Council Pakistan website.

Master’s Applicants

Candidates applying for support towards an eligible master’s programme can submit their application through the dedicated master’s application portal:

Apply here: https://www.research.net/r/ZC8YPKJ

Master’s applicants should carefully review the document titled “Scotland Pakistan Scholarship FAQs-MASTER’s 2026-27” for detailed guidance relating to postgraduate applications.

Important Documents Applicants Should Review

The British Council has made several official guidance documents available to prospective applicants.

Candidates are strongly advised to review the relevant documents before submitting their application. These include:

  1. Scotland Pakistan Scholarship FAQs and Bachelors 2026
  2. Scotland Pakistan Scholarship FAQs-General 2026-27
  3. Scotland Pakistan Scholarship FAQs-MASTER’s 2026-27

The general FAQ document provides broader information about the scholarship, while the bachelor’s and master’s documents provide information relevant to the respective levels of study.

Applicants should rely on these official documents for detailed guidance and clarification about programme requirements.

Scotland Pakistan Scholarships 2026 Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026 has been extended to 15 September 2026.

Candidates who meet the eligibility requirements should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications.

Submitting early can provide additional time to address technical problems, missing information or other issues that could arise during the application process.

Application Deadline: 15 September 2026

Key Information at a Glance

Here are the major details prospective applicants should know:

  • Programme: Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026
  • Funded by: Scottish Government
  • Administered by: British Council Pakistan
  • Study location: Pakistan
  • University requirement: HEC-recognised university in Pakistan
  • Study levels: Four-year bachelor’s degree and up to two-year master’s/MPhil degree
  • Eligible applicants: Female Pakistani nationals currently residing in Pakistan
  • Bachelor’s duration supported: Four years
  • Master’s/MPhil duration supported: Maximum of two years
  • Eligible subjects: Education, Sustainable Energy, Food Security and Agriculture, Health Sciences, STEM and Climate
  • Financial support: Eligible tuition fees, university hostel costs where applicable, specified home-to-university travel and research-related support for master’s students
  • Application deadline: 15 September 2026

Why Pakistani Women Should Consider This Opportunity

For eligible students, the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls can provide meaningful financial support during university education.

The programme is particularly noteworthy because it addresses several costs associated with studying rather than focusing exclusively on tuition.

Depending on an applicant’s circumstances and level of study, support may extend to accommodation, travel and, for master’s students, research-related costs.

The scholarship also concentrates on disciplines with significant relevance to development and future workforce needs, including STEM, health sciences, sustainable energy, climate, agriculture, food security and education.

For women from rural communities, women with disabilities and women from minority groups, the programme may provide an especially important pathway towards accessing and continuing higher education.

Important Advice Before Applying

Prospective applicants should carefully confirm that they satisfy the scholarship conditions before completing the application.

In particular, candidates should:

  1. Confirm that they are eligible under the nationality and residency requirements.
  2. Ensure they have a confirmed admission offer from an HEC-recognised university in Pakistan.
  3. Verify that their degree is within one of the specified subject areas.
  4. Use the correct application link for their study level.
  5. Read the relevant bachelor’s or master’s FAQ document.
  6. Review the general scholarship FAQ for additional information.
  7. Ensure all information submitted in the application is accurate and complete.
  8. Submit the application before the 15 September 2026 deadline.

Applicants should also retain copies of their submitted information and any supporting documents for their records.

APPLY NOW

About the British Council’s Role

The British Council administers the Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls scheme in Pakistan.

As the programme administrator, the British Council coordinates with selected scholarship recipients and participating universities. This coordination may take place directly or through nominated university focal persons.

Applicants should therefore refer to the British Council Pakistan’s official scholarship information and guidance documents when seeking authoritative information about the programme.

Conclusion

The Scotland Pakistan Scholarships for Young Women and Girls 2026 offer an important opportunity for Pakistani women seeking financial assistance to pursue higher education at HEC-recognised universities across Pakistan.

Funded by the Scottish Government and administered by the British Council, the programme supports eligible four-year bachelor’s and up to two-year master’s/MPhil programmes across six priority areas: Education, Sustainable Energy, Food Security and Agriculture, Health Sciences, STEM and Climate.

Financial assistance can include eligible tuition fees, university hostel costs where applicable and travel between home and university twice per year for students living in on-campus hostels. Master’s scholars may additionally receive funding to support research work involving access to appropriate laboratories, equipment and tools.

Female Pakistani nationals currently living in Pakistan who have a confirmed admission offer from an HEC-recognised university and are pursuing an eligible programme should carefully review the official requirements and consider applying.

Young women with disabilities and those from rural areas and minority groups are particularly encouraged to apply.

With the deadline now extended, eligible candidates have until 15 September 2026 to submit their applications.

Bachelor’s applicants can apply at:

https://www.research.net/r/WZQB3D5

Master’s applicants can apply at:

https://www.research.net/r/ZC8YPKJ

Applicants should also visit the British Council Pakistan website and review the official Scotland Pakistan Scholarship FAQs for their respective level of study before completing their application.

Visit the OFY website for more global Scholarship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Third Wave Fund Mobilize Power Fund 2026, a rapid-response funding opportunity designed to support gender justice organizations and groups in the United States and U.S. territories that need to respond quickly to unexpected, time-sensitive opportunities or threats affecting their communities, movement-building activities, or organizing conditions.

Through the Mobilize Power Fund, eligible organizations can receive grants of up to $10,000 USD, while partnerships or coalitions involving two or more groups can request up to $20,000 USD. The programme is specifically intended for organizations that need to significantly adapt or pivot their work because of an unforeseen incident or change in circumstances that occurred within the previous six months.

The Mobilize Power Fund is not intended to finance ordinary organizational activities or compensate for routine budget shortages. Instead, it provides flexible resources that enable gender justice movements to respond to rapidly changing circumstances through activities such as community organizing, direct action, healing justice, mutual aid, conflict resolution, legal or bail support, leadership development, and unexpected legislative or ballot initiative campaigns.

The September 2026 application cycle is currently open, with applications due by September 8, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time. Organizations that cannot apply during the September cycle will have another opportunity when the October cycle opens on September 9, 2026.

About the Third Wave Fund Mobilize Power Fund

The Mobilize Power Fund is a rapid-response grantmaking programme operated by Third Wave Fund to provide gender justice organizations with resources when unforeseen developments require an immediate or significant change in their work.

The fund recognizes that movement-building does not always happen according to predictable schedules. Organizations working directly with communities affected by gender oppression can encounter unexpected political developments, safety concerns, community crises, organizing opportunities, legislative changes, or other circumstances requiring an immediate response.

Rather than requiring organizations to wait for conventional long-term funding cycles, the Mobilize Power Fund provides a mechanism through which qualifying groups can seek resources to respond to these situations.

Third Wave Fund describes the programme as a resource for organizations needing to adapt or pivot their work when faced with unanticipated and time-sensitive opportunities or threats to their movement-building work and organizing conditions.

How Much Funding Is Available?

The amount organizations can request depends on whether they are applying individually as a group or organization or jointly through a partnership or coalition.

Funding is available as follows:

  • Individual organizations or groups: Up to $10,000 USD
  • Partnerships or coalitions involving two or more groups: Up to $20,000 USD

This makes the programme particularly relevant for organizations that require relatively small but timely grants to respond to circumstances that could not reasonably have been anticipated through their normal programming or budgeting processes.

What Is the Purpose of the Mobilize Power Fund?

The Mobilize Power Fund was established around the understanding that effective movements need the ability not only to plan long-term strategies but also to respond to immediate opportunities and threats.

Third Wave Fund explains that the programme was created because movements need flexible and responsive funding to both respond to and heal from urgent circumstances.

The first iteration of the Mobilize Power Fund supported organizers responding to HB2, the North Carolina legislation widely known as the “Bathroom Bill,” in 2016.

The fund has subsequently developed into a broader rapid-response funding mechanism for qualifying gender justice organizations confronting unexpected developments.

Who Is the Mobilize Power Fund For?

The Mobilize Power Fund supports gender justice organizations and groups whose work is rooted in and accountable to communities directly affected by gender oppression.

These organizations must be adapting or pivoting their work in response to an unexpected and time-sensitive opportunity or threat affecting their movement work or organizing conditions.

This means applicants should be able to clearly demonstrate both:

  1. Their existing connection and accountability to the communities they serve; and
  2. Why a recent development requires them to substantially change or expand their planned activities.

Geographic Eligibility: Where Must Applicants Be Based?

The Mobilize Power Fund is geographically restricted.

Third Wave Fund states that funding is provided only within the United States and U.S. territories.

Eligible locations include:

  • United States
  • American Samoa
  • Guam
  • Northern Mariana Islands
  • Puerto Rico
  • U.S. Virgin Islands

Groups based outside the United States and U.S. territories are not prioritized by the fund.

International organizations operating entirely outside these eligible geographic areas should therefore not consider this a global grant opportunity.

Organizational Budget Requirement

One of the most important eligibility requirements is the organization’s budget.

To qualify for a Mobilize Power Fund grant, an organization must have an annual organizational budget of less than $500,000 USD.

Third Wave Fund additionally prioritizes organizations and groups that:

  • Operate in areas where access to philanthropic resources is limited; and
  • Do not have access to 501(c)(3) status or fiscal sponsorship.

The lack of 501(c)(3) status or fiscal sponsorship therefore does not automatically exclude a group from consideration. In fact, organizations facing these structural funding barriers are specifically identified as a priority.

Core Eligibility and Selection Criteria

Third Wave Fund identifies several important areas that organizations should demonstrate through their applications.

1. Accountability to Communities

Leadership and decision-making structures should demonstrate meaningful accountability to communities directly affected by gender oppression.

The programme specifically references communities including:

  • Young women of color
  • Trans youth
  • Queer youth
  • Intersex youth
  • Gender non-conforming youth
  • People of color under the age of 35

Organizations should demonstrate alignment between their leadership, governance structures, and the communities they serve.

2. Gender Justice

Applicants need to demonstrate a clear gender justice analysis.

Their political analysis should explain how the issue being addressed connects to one or more areas such as:

  • Patriarchy
  • Transphobia
  • Homophobia
  • Gender inequity
  • Gender-based violence

Simply responding to an urgent situation is therefore not sufficient. The organization should also demonstrate how that situation relates to gender justice.

3. Rapid Response

The organization must be responding to a specific incident or change in circumstances that occurred within the previous six months.

The situation should require the organization to significantly pivot from its ongoing and regularly planned activities.

4. Community Power Building

The strategies and activities proposed should strengthen the organizing and movement-building power of the communities involved.

The proposed activities should also directly contribute to the overall objectives described in the application.

5. Organizational Need

Organizations must have budgets below $500,000 USD to qualify.

Priority is additionally given to organizations operating in areas with limited access to philanthropic resources and organizations without access to 501(c)(3) status or fiscal sponsorship.

What Types of Activities Are Prioritized?

The Mobilize Power Fund is intended to respond to unexpected circumstances rather than support routine activities.

Third Wave Fund identifies several examples of work that may receive priority, including:

  • Unexpected and time-sensitive community organizing
  • Direct action
  • Participatory Action Research
  • Healing justice work
  • Conflict mediation
  • Conflict resolution
  • Legal fees
  • Bail fees
  • Marches
  • Rallies
  • Leadership training
  • Skills building
  • Mutual aid
  • Unexpected legislative campaigns
  • Unexpected ballot initiative campaigns

These examples illustrate the programme’s emphasis on rapidly mobilizing resources where organizations need to respond to a new circumstance rather than simply continue activities they had already planned.

What Types of Applications Are Not Prioritized?

Organizations should carefully consider whether their proposed activities genuinely fit the rapid-response purpose of the fund before applying.

Third Wave Fund states that the Mobilize Power Fund does not prioritize applications involving:

  • Budget shortfalls
  • Ongoing or regularly scheduled programmes
  • Start-up or seed costs
  • Fundraising
  • Previously planned campaigns
  • Long-term campaigns
  • Projects led by individuals
  • Charity
  • Groups based outside the United States and U.S. territories

For the purposes of this programme, Third Wave Fund defines long-term programming as programming extending beyond six months.

Applicants should therefore clearly establish that their proposed work represents a genuine response or pivot rather than an attempt to finance existing activities.

Mobilize Power Fund 2026 Application Deadlines

The Mobilize Power Fund is no longer accepting applications on a rolling basis.

Applications must instead be submitted during specific funding cycles, and all deadlines are at 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

June 2026 Cycle

Applications opened: May 5, 2026
Deadline: June 2, 2026

July 2026 Cycle

Applications opened: June 3, 2026
Deadline: July 7, 2026

September 2026 Cycle

Applications opened: August 5, 2026
Deadline: September 8, 2026

October 2026 Cycle

Applications open: September 9, 2026
Deadline: October 6, 2026

Organizations planning to apply should make sure they submit within an active funding cycle.

Application Materials Required

Applicants need to gather several pieces of information and documentation before completing their submission.

Basic Information

Applicants must provide:

  • Contact information
  • A description of the group or organization
  • A brief one-to-two-sentence description of the application

Group or Organizational Budget

Applicants should provide the group’s or organization’s total budget for the current calendar or fiscal year, where applicable.

Third Wave Fund provides an organizational budget template for this purpose.

Independent 501(c)(3) Organizations

Applicants operating as independent 501(c)(3) organizations should provide their organization’s IRS letter.

Fiscally Sponsored Organizations

Fiscally sponsored applicants should provide:

  1. The fiscal sponsor’s organizational budget
  2. The fiscal sponsor’s 501(c)(3) IRS letter
  3. A current fiscal sponsor agreement signed by both parties

Applicants must also provide responses to the required application narrative questions.

Three Ways to Complete the Application Narrative

An important feature of the Mobilize Power Fund application is the flexibility provided for completing the narrative component.

Applicants can provide their narrative through:

  1. A written application
  2. A selfie video submission
  3. A Zoom or phone interview

Written Applications

Written narratives should be no longer than one page and must be uploaded through the grant portal.

Video Applications

Video narratives can be up to 10 minutes long.

Applicants should upload a link to their video through the grant portal.

Phone or Zoom Applications

Organizations wishing to complete their narrative through an interview should contact Third Wave Fund to schedule a Zoom or phone call.

Interview calls must be scheduled and completed at least one week before the relevant application deadline.

Because Third Wave Fund has limited staff capacity, it may not be able to accommodate every interview request.

The fund aims to prioritize phone interviews for:

  • Groups for which a written narrative is inaccessible
  • Groups led by BIPOC trans people
  • Groups led by young people under 25
  • Groups without tax status
  • Spanish-speaking groups
  • Groups based in U.S. territories

Mobilize Power Fund 2026 Narrative Questions

Third Wave Fund updated its narrative proposal questions in April 2026. Previous applicants should therefore carefully review the current questions rather than relying on earlier versions of their applications.

Applicants are asked to address the following areas:

1. Purpose and Structure

Describe the purpose and structure of the organization and provide an overview of its regular activities.

Partnerships or coalitions should briefly describe each participating organization.

2. Accountability

Explain how the organization’s leadership is rooted in and accountable to the communities it serves, including young women of color and trans, queer, intersex, and gender non-conforming youth under 35.

Applicants should explain how their leadership aligns with the communities being served.

3. Context

Explain the specific incident or change in circumstances that occurred within the previous six months.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate how their proposed response relates to gender justice.

4. Pivot

Explain how the organization has pivoted or intends to pivot in response to the situation.

Applicants should explain how the proposed response differs from their existing work and provide a detailed timeline showing how their strategies and activities address the relevant incident or change.

5. Impact

Describe the impact the organization hopes to achieve within approximately six to eight months.

Applicants should also explain how young BIWOC and/or TIGNCBIPOC communities will benefit from the proposed work.

6. Partnerships

Applicants submitting a partnership or coalition proposal must explain the role each participating organization will play.

How to Apply for the Mobilize Power Fund 2026

Applications are submitted through the Proteus Fund Fluxx online grant portal.

Step 1: Access the Portal

Visit:

proteus.fluxx.io

Step 2: Create or Access Your Account

The procedure depends on whether you are a new or returning applicant.

Returning Applicants and Grantees

Organizations that have previously applied to a Third Wave Fund or Proteus Fund grant programme but have not used the new application system should use the Forgot Password function with their email address to regain access.

New Applicants

New applicants should request a new account at least three business days before the application deadline to allow time for approval.

Applicants should:

  1. Select “Register Now.”
  2. Complete all required fields on the registration form.
  3. Select “Submit Request.”
  4. Wait for a verification email.
  5. Follow the verification link to create a password.
  6. Log into the application system.
  7. Select “Open Grant Opportunities.”
  8. Choose “Third Wave Fund – Mobilize Power Fund.”
  9. Begin the application.

The verification link sent to new applicants is valid for only 24 hours.

Third Wave Fund also recommends setting up the portal account in advance to allow time to resolve potential technical difficulties.

What Happens After Submitting an Application?

After submitting an application through Fluxx, applicants should receive a confirmation email.

The application will also appear under “Submitted Requests” within the applicant’s Fluxx account.

If Third Wave Fund requires clarification, additional information, or supporting documentation, the applicant will be contacted through the email address connected to their account.

The application may then be moved to “Requests to Edit”, allowing the applicant to review what additional information is required and submit the requested changes.

Applicants can also use the Fluxx portal to follow their application through the decision-making process.

When Will Applicants Receive a Decision?

Applicants are generally notified within four to six weeks after the monthly review deadline.

The notification may indicate that the application:

  • Has been recommended for funding
  • Has not been recommended for funding
  • Requires additional follow-up information

Third Wave Fund indicates that grant payments typically occur up to two months after the monthly review deadline, after the applicant has been notified and all necessary paperwork has been completed.

Payments are generally made through ACH direct deposit where applicable.

Third Wave Fund notes that it may be able to process requests more quickly in emergency situations.

Accessibility and Applicant Support

Third Wave Fund aims to make the application process accessible.

English applications use a screen-reader-compatible online portal. Applicants who require accommodations or have feedback concerning accessibility can contact the organization directly.

For application questions or support:

Email: mpf@thirdwavefund.org
Phone: 917-387-1262 x 920

For technical problems involving the Fluxx application system, applicants can contact:

fluxx@proteusfund.org

Important Tips for Applicants

Organizations interested in applying should carefully evaluate their circumstances before beginning an application.

First, make sure the issue being addressed occurred within the previous six months and represents an unexpected development rather than a previously planned activity.

Applicants should then demonstrate why this development requires a significant pivot from their organization’s normal work.

The proposal should also clearly establish the relationship between the issue and gender justice, particularly areas such as gender inequity, patriarchy, transphobia, homophobia or gender-based violence.

Organizations should demonstrate meaningful accountability to the communities they serve and explain how the proposed activities will build community organizing and movement power.

Applicants should also remember that:

  • Organizational budgets must be below $500,000.
  • Individual organizations or groups can request up to $10,000.
  • Partnerships or coalitions of at least two groups can request up to $20,000.
  • The proposed response should address an incident or change occurring within the previous six months.
  • Long-term programming extending beyond six months is not prioritized.
  • New applicants should request a Fluxx account at least three business days before the deadline.
  • Phone or Zoom interviews must be scheduled and completed at least one week before the application deadline.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Third Wave Fund Mobilize Power Fund 2026 offers an important rapid-response funding opportunity for gender justice organizations and groups facing unexpected circumstances that require immediate adaptation, organizing, or action.

With grants of up to $10,000 USD for individual organizations and groups and up to $20,000 USD for partnerships or coalitions, the programme can provide timely financial support for organizations undertaking activities such as direct action, mutual aid, healing justice, conflict resolution, legal or bail support, leadership development, community organizing, and unexpected legislative or ballot initiative campaigns.

However, this is a highly targeted funding programme. Applicants must be based within the United States or U.S. territories, have organizational budgets below $500,000, demonstrate accountability to communities directly impacted by gender oppression, and be responding to a specific incident or change in circumstances that occurred within the previous six months.

Organizations interested in the September funding cycle should prepare their applications as soon as possible. The September 2026 deadline is September 8, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time. The October cycle will then open on September 9, with a final deadline of October 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities.
