item.content:encoded:
Consilium traineeships are now open for applications. Twice a year, the Council offers 5-month paid traineeships in Brussels, providing graduates with the opportunity to gain valuable insights into the work of the European Union and first-hand experience of EU policy-making.

Key Summary

  • Opportunity: Consilium traineeships
  • Organisation: Council of the European Union
  • Location: Brussels, Belgium 🇧🇪
  • Date of closing of application (Brussels Time): 15/09/2026 12:00
  • Date of the start of traineeship: 01/02/2027
  • Duration: 5 months
  • Traineeship grant: €1,538.16
  • Traineeship positions: 110 positions available each year
  • Type: Paid traineeship
  • Fields: Policy, law, administration, communications, translation, IT and other areas
  • Eligibility: EU citizenship, a bachelor’s degree or higher, required language skills and other eligibility criteria
  • Languages: A very good knowledge of English or French and of at least one other EU language
  • Previous experience: No previous work experience at another EU institution

👉 APPLY NOW: https://consilium.gestmax.eu/2279/1/paid-traineeship-february-june-2027/en_US

The traineeship programme

The Consilium traineeship programme allows graduates from a range of backgrounds to gain first-hand experience of EU policy-making.

The Council offers traineeships in different areas, such as:

  • Policy
  • Law
  • Administration
  • Communications
  • Translation
  • IT

110 traineeship positions are available each year.

The programme offers an opportunity to gain valuable insights into the work of the European Union, contribute to the Council’s daily activities and learn from colleagues and advisors.

Applications are now open!

Applications are now open for the Consilium traineeships running from 1 February to 30 June 2027.

You can apply until:

📅 15 September 2026, at 12:00 (Brussels time)

APPLY NOW: https://consilium.gestmax.eu/2279/1/paid-traineeship-february-june-2027/en_US

Who can apply?

Consilium traineeships are open to everybody, subject to certain eligibility criteria.

🇪🇺 EU citizenship

Applicants must meet the programme’s EU citizenship requirements.

🎓 A bachelor’s degree or higher

Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or higher.

🌍 Language requirements

Applicants must have a very good knowledge of English or French and of at least one other EU language.

💼 Previous EU institutional experience

Applicants must have no previous work experience at another EU institution, subject to the detailed eligibility requirements of the programme.

👉 Who can apply for a traineeship: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/who-can-apply-for-a-traineeship/

What is offered

The Consilium traineeship programme gives young professionals the opportunity to:

  • Gain insights into the work of the EU
  • Be involved in the Council’s daily activities
  • Learn from colleagues and advisors
  • Contribute to shaping important decisions
  • Gain practical experience of EU policy-making

Traineeships are paid and include allowances and other benefits.

👉 Your traineeship: tasks, grants, allowances: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/your-traineeship-tasks-grants-allowances/

Positive action programme for trainees with a disability

Each year, the Council reserves up to six traineeships for EU nationals with a recognised disability.

The programme offers participants a unique insight into EU policy and law-making, whilst providing them with special workplace arrangements, as necessary.

👉 Positive action programme for trainees with a disability: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/positive-action-programme-for-trainees-with-a-disability/

Traineeships for students from national administration schools

In addition to the general traineeship programme, the Council offers traineeships for students from national administration schools.

These traineeships provide students with unique insights into the processes and policies of the EU institutions.

They last between two and five months.

👉 Traineeships for students from national administration schools: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/traineeships-for-students-of-national-administration-schools/

Traineeship calendar

The Council offers traineeships twice a year.

First traineeship period: February to June

The first traineeship period runs from 1 February to 30 June.

  • Applications: Mid-July to mid-September
  • Selection and interviews: October to December
  • Traineeship: February to June

For the current application round, the traineeship will run from:

1 February to 30 June 2027

Second traineeship period: September to January

The second traineeship period runs from 1 September to 31 January.

  • Applications: February and March
  • Selection of candidates: April to June
  • Traineeship: September to January

How to apply for a traineeship

Interested candidates should review the eligibility requirements and submit their application through the Council’s online application system.

👉 Apply for the Consilium Traineeship: https://consilium.gestmax.eu/2279/1/paid-traineeship-february-june-2027/en_US

👉 How to apply for a traineeship: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/how-to-apply-for-a-traineeship/

Frequently asked questions

Candidates can consult the Council’s frequently asked questions for more information about the Consilium traineeships, including eligibility, applications and the traineeship programme.

👉 Traineeships: frequently asked questions: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/frequently-asked-questions/

Council rules on traineeships

The Consilium traineeship programme is governed by the Council’s rules on traineeships.

👉 Decision No. 14/25 on traineeships: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/media/5gicvwb1/de00014en25.pdf

 

Traineeships: frequently asked questions

Answers to the most popular questions regarding traineeships at the Council.

Please find below the most frequently asked questions. You can find the full list of questions and answers in the following document:

  • Frequently asked questions – traineeships 

If you don’t find an answer to your question, you can contact the traineeships office:

  • traineeships@consilium.europa.eu 

Application

Can I do a traineeship during the summer?

No. Traineeships are not offered during the summer.

Traineeships are only possible during the two official periods:

  • February to June (first period)
  • September to January (second period)

Are spontaneous applications considered?

No. All applications for a traineeship must follow the application procedure described on the website.

I am a citizen from a candidate country. Can I apply for a traineeship?

No. Traineeships are only open to candidates from candidate countries that have concluded EU accession negotiations. As there are currently no candidate countries that have concluded negotiations, it’s not possible for their citizens to apply.

What proof do I need of EU citizenship?

Applicants must hold a passport or ID card from an EU country. Residence permits are not accepted.

I have not yet received my bachelor’s degree. Can I apply for a paid traineeship?

To be eligible, the candidate must obtain a diploma at bachelor (BA) level or higher by the closing date for applications at the latest.

Can I apply for a traineeship in different EU institutions at the same time?

You can apply for a traineeship at different EU institutions at the same time if you fulfil the eligibility criteria.

Selection procedure

How are trainees selected?

Trainees are selected based on merit, considering the information provided in the application form.

Candidates might be interviewed by telephone or online. In this case the traineeships office will contact candidates beforehand to arrange a suitable time. Where candidates are judged to be of equal merit, the traineeships office endeavours to secure a healthy geographic (i.e. as many nationalities represented as possible) and gender balance (aiming for 40% of the underrepresented gender) of selected trainees. Applications are scrutinised and compared against the profile sought by the various departments of the General Secretariat of the Council.

Do I have to send copies of certificates concerning my language skills?

You do not need to send any certificates at the application stage.

If you are selected for the traineeship, you will need to prove all language skills that you mention in your application form.

If you do not have a specific document (diploma from language studies, copy of evaluation reports including the language or other proof), you will need to write, date and sign a short declaration explaining the circumstances justifying the lack of supporting documents (e.g. a course, your second mother tongue, living in a country, etc.).

After selection

Should I provide translations of supporting documents?

No. Supporting documents are accepted in all official languages of the EU. It is helpful to also provide an English or French version of diplomas, if available.

Do the copies of supporting documents need to be certified as authentic copies of the originals?

No. Supporting documents need to be sent by email. There is no need to provide certified copies. Upon arrival trainees might be asked to present the originals of supporting documents.

During the traineeship

Am I entitled to annual leave?

Trainees are entitled to 2 days leave per worked month, in addition to public holidays and days when Council offices are closed.

Health insurance is mandatory. Is the European health insurance card for my country enough?

Yes. We accept the copy of your European health insurance card as proof. It is your responsibility to check the cover it offers. In the absence of other cover (e.g. European health insurance card), trainees can opt for health insurance through the Council. In this case, paid trainees pay circa €20 per month, which corresponds to one third of the premium, and the Council pays the remaining two thirds.

Are trainees insured?

All trainees benefit from accident insurance.

Financial aspects

How much is the grant?

Presently the grant is €1 538.16 net/month.

Does the Council of the European Union cover the cost of travel from my place of residence to Brussels?

Trainees receive a travel allowance as a contribution towards their travel expenses. Trainees who are recruited from a place more than 50 km from Brussels are entitled to a contribution towards travel expenses at the beginning and at the end of the traineeship.

You must complete at least half of the period of your traineeship in order to be entitled. No requests for change of address will be accepted after the signature of the traineeship agreement by the Council.

Related documents and publications

  • Frequently asked questions – traineeships 
  • Decision 14/25 on traineeships 
  • Description of domains 
  • Description of domains by trainees 

Apply now

If you are a graduate interested in gaining first-hand experience of EU policy-making and valuable insights into the work of the European Union, the Consilium traineeship programme offers an opportunity to work in Brussels and contribute to the Council’s daily activities.

Applications close on 15 September 2026 at 12:00 (Brussels time).

👉 APPLY NOW: https://consilium.gestmax.eu/2279/1/paid-traineeship-february-june-2027/en_US

 

Source: https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/general-secretariat/careers/traineeships/?utm_source=linkedin.com&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=20260813-gsc-traineeship&utm_content=visual-carousel

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Migrant Women Press Emerging Women Journalists Fellowship 2026–27, a professional development programme supporting emerging women journalists, media practitioners and communications professionals from migrant and adversely racialised backgrounds who are based in Scotland.

The Fellowship has been designed to help participants bridge the gap between education and professional access to the media industry. It combines journalism training, one-to-one mentoring, editorial development, publication opportunities, networking and an industry placement, giving Fellows a structured pathway for strengthening their skills and building professional confidence.

For the 2026–27 cohort, Migrant Women Press plans to select:

Eight Fellows

The programme will run from:

October 2026 to April 2027

Applications close on:

Sunday, 13 September 2026 at 11:59 PM

Applicants are expected to be informed of the outcome by:

28 September 2026

Selected Fellows will receive a total £600 stipend, professional journalism training, mentoring from an experienced journalist or media professional, editorial support to produce an original story, a three-month part-time industry placement, publication opportunities and professional networking.

The Fellowship is specifically designed to build pathways into journalism for migrant and racialised women in Scotland.

About the Migrant Women Press Emerging Women Journalists Fellowship

The MWP Emerging Women Journalists Fellowship is a journalism training and career-development programme created by Migrant Women Press CIC, an independent nonprofit media organisation led by migrant women and women of colour.

Migrant Women Press works to amplify underrepresented voices through journalism and storytelling while using an intersectional approach to promote a more inclusive and representative media environment.

The Fellowship responds to barriers that migrant and racialised women can face when trying to enter or progress within journalism and media.

Rather than focusing only on formal classroom learning, the programme combines several forms of professional development:

  • Journalism skills training
  • Editorial support
  • Mentoring
  • Practical reporting
  • Publication
  • Industry experience
  • Networking
  • Career development

The goal is to help Fellows move from academic or early-stage experience toward more confident participation in professional media.

Fellowship Duration

The 2026–27 Fellowship begins in:

Early October 2026

and finishes in:

April 2027

The broad programme structure is:

  • October 2026: Fellowship induction and mentor matching
  • October 2026–January 2027: Training, mentoring, reporting, writing and editorial development
  • January 2027: Online story publication
  • February 2027: Fellowship print magazine prepared
  • February–April 2027: Industry placements
  • April 2027: Final Fellowship event in Glasgow

The Applicant Guide confirms that the programme begins in early October and continues until April 2027.

What the Fellowship Offers

The programme provides a comprehensive package of professional development opportunities.

1. Professional Journalism Training

Selected Fellows participate in professional journalism training delivered by:

  • Journalists
  • Media professionals
  • Academics
  • Industry experts

The training is intended to help participants strengthen practical reporting skills while also engaging critically with ethics, representation and responsible journalism.

The programme combines technical journalism development with discussion of how journalists represent people and communities in the media.

Journalism Training Topics

The planned programme includes areas such as:

  • Writing journalism articles
  • Multimedia journalism
  • Fact-checking and verification
  • Introduction to investigative journalism
  • Media law and ethics
  • AI in journalism
  • Primary prevention of men’s violence against women and girls and the role of the media
  • Representation of “the Other” in the media

Training is expected to run primarily from:

October 2026 to January 2027

with approximately:

Two sessions per month

Most sessions will take place:

Online and mainly in the evenings

This structure is intended to make participation more accessible to Fellows who may also be:

  • Studying
  • Working
  • Caring for others

Trauma-Informed Reporting Training

A particularly important component of the Fellowship is its focus on:

Trauma-informed journalism

Migrant Women Press emphasizes that journalists have a responsibility to approach sensitive stories with:

  • Care
  • Respect
  • Awareness of potential harm
  • Sensitivity toward people who have experienced trauma

This may be especially relevant when reporting on:

  • Violence
  • Abuse
  • Loss
  • Distress
  • Migrant communities
  • Racialised communities
  • Victims and survivors

The training aims to help Fellows understand how journalistic choices can affect the people whose stories they report.

Participants will explore how to:

  • Avoid causing additional harm
  • Interview sensitively
  • Represent people with dignity
  • Respect agency
  • Challenge harmful narratives

The trauma-informed reporting training is expected to be completed online at the Fellow’s own pace by January 2027, followed by a live question-and-answer session.

It is also CPD Certified, with:

Two hours of Continuing Professional Development accreditation

awarded on completion.

One-to-One Professional Mentoring

Every Fellow will be matched with an experienced:

  • Journalist
  • Editor
  • Producer
  • Media professional

The mentoring relationship is intended to provide professional guidance throughout the Fellowship.

Fellows will generally have:

One online one-to-one meeting with their mentor each month.

What Mentoring Can Include

Mentors may support Fellows with:

  • Refining their story idea
  • Developing journalistic skills
  • Reviewing at least the first full story draft
  • Career guidance
  • Industry insight
  • Professional opportunities where possible
  • Professional networking
  • Discussing career goals
  • Discussing challenges
  • Planning next steps

The programme also makes clear that mentors are not responsible for finding Fellows a job or fully editing their work.

Fellows are expected to:

  • Take initiative
  • Prepare for meetings
  • Communicate professionally
  • Be open to constructive criticism
  • Respect mentors’ time and professional boundaries

Produce and Publish Your Own Fellowship Story

Producing an original journalistic feature is a central component of the programme.

Each Fellow will develop an original feature story of approximately:

1,000 words

The final story will normally include:

  • Research
  • At least two interviews
  • A short multimedia component

Applicants are asked to pitch one story idea as part of the Fellowship application.

This idea will become the starting point for the reporting project if the applicant is selected.

Story Topic Requirement

The proposed story should have:

A clear connection to Scotland or communities living in Scotland.

Applicants are not expected to submit a perfectly developed professional pitch.

Migrant Women Press is more interested in:

  • The strength of the idea
  • Curiosity
  • Relevance
  • Reporting potential
  • The applicant’s thinking about how the story could be developed

Selected Fellows will have opportunities to strengthen and refine their original idea through:

  • Mentoring
  • Training
  • Reporting
  • Editorial support

Story Development Timeline

The Fellowship provides a structured editorial pathway.

October

Fellows develop and refine their story idea with their mentor.

They begin:

  • Reporting plans
  • Research
  • Interviews

October–November

Fellows continue reporting and writing.

They submit a:

First full draft

to their mentor.

November–December

Fellows revise the story based on mentor feedback and submit a:

Second draft

to the Fellowship editor.

December–January

Fellows work with the editor to:

  • Respond to professional editorial feedback
  • Fact-check
  • Complete revisions

January

Stories successfully completing the editorial process are prepared for:

Online publication

February

Published stories are prepared for inclusion in the Fellowship’s:

Print magazine

The visual timeline on page 7 of the Applicant Guide illustrates this progression from story idea to online and print publication.

£600 Fellowship Stipend

Each selected Fellow will receive:

£600

The stipend recognizes:

  • Participation
  • Time commitment
  • Reporting
  • Research
  • Story production

The £600 is paid in:

Two instalments

First instalment

£300 in October 2026

This is paid at the beginning of the Fellowship after the Fellowship Agreement has been completed.

Second instalment

£300 toward the end of January 2027

This is paid after the Fellow has completed the editorial process and submitted the final story for publication.

Applicants should therefore understand that the stipend is connected to participation and programme progress rather than being a single payment made before the programme begins.

Three-Month Industry Placement

Another major component of the Fellowship is a:

Three-month, part-time industry placement

The placement will normally run from:

February to April 2027

and may take place with a:

  • Media organisation
  • Newsroom
  • Communications team

Industry Placement Workload

Placements will normally require approximately:

One or two days per week

They may be:

  • In person
  • Online
  • Hybrid

The exact arrangement will be agreed between:

  • The Fellow
  • Host organisation
  • Migrant Women Press

and will take into account both the Fellow’s circumstances and the host organisation’s working arrangements.

What Fellows May Do During Their Placement

Possible activities include:

  • Editorial research
  • Reporting
  • Newsroom shadowing
  • Joining editorial meetings
  • Story development
  • Fact-checking
  • Feature production
  • Multimedia production
  • Podcast work
  • Audio production
  • Newsletter production
  • Social media
  • Audience engagement
  • Communications work
  • Press work

The purpose is to help Fellows understand how journalism and communications teams operate professionally.

Is the Industry Placement Paid Separately?

No additional payment from the placement host should normally be expected.

The placement forms part of the overall Fellowship.

However, Migrant Women Press states that:

Reasonable travel expenses required for an in-person placement will be covered.

Professional Networking

Fellows also receive opportunities to build professional relationships with:

  • Journalists
  • Editors
  • Media organisations
  • Mentors
  • Other Fellows
  • Previous Fellowship participants

Networking forms an important part of the programme because access to professional contacts can be particularly valuable for emerging journalists trying to enter the media industry.

Final Fellowship Event in Glasgow

The Fellowship concludes in:

April 2027

with a final event in:

Glasgow

The event will bring together:

  • Fellows
  • Mentors
  • Industry placement partners
  • Supporters

Fellows will also participate in programme evaluation and become part of the:

MWP Fellowship alumni community.

Who Can Apply?

The Fellowship is intended for emerging women journalists and media or communications professionals from:

Migrant and adversely racialised backgrounds

Applicants must also be based in:

Scotland

for the duration of the Fellowship.

Academic and Career Eligibility

Applicants should normally meet one of the following conditions:

  • Currently studying journalism
  • Currently studying media
  • Currently studying communications
  • Currently studying a related subject

or:

  • Have graduated from a relevant programme within the last three years

What If You Graduated More Than Three Years Ago?

There is some flexibility.

Migrant Women Press states that people who graduated more than three years ago but are still at an early stage of their journalism or media career because circumstances affected their ability to enter or progress in the industry are encouraged to:

Contact Migrant Women Press before applying.

This recognizes that career progression is not always linear.

Migrant and Racialised Background Eligibility

The programme welcomes women from a range of migration experiences.

The application information specifically welcomes:

  • International students
  • Refugees
  • People seeking asylum
  • First-generation migrants
  • Second-generation migrants
  • Third-generation migrants

The key requirement is that applicants identify as coming from a:

Migrant and/or adversely racialised background.

Trans Women Are Welcome

The Fellowship is explicitly:

Trans-inclusive

and:

Trans women are welcome to apply.

This is an important part of the programme’s inclusion policy.

Do You Need Professional Journalism Experience?

No substantial professional experience is required.

The application process is intentionally designed to assess:

  • Potential
  • Motivation
  • Curiosity
  • Ideas
  • Interests

rather than simply measuring how much professional experience an applicant already has.

Applicants are not given an automatic advantage because they:

  • Have more professional experience
  • Have already been published by a major organisation
  • Have had greater access to industry opportunities

This makes the Fellowship particularly relevant to people who have not yet had extensive professional media access.

Previous Work Example

Applicants need to provide:

One example of previous work

However, it does not need to have been professionally published.

Possible examples may include:

  • Academic work
  • Student journalism
  • Independent work
  • Community media
  • Other relevant work

This allows emerging journalists who have not yet built a conventional professional portfolio to apply.

What Will the Application Ask?

Candidates should be prepared to answer questions concerning:

  • Why they want to join the Fellowship
  • What matters to them about journalism, media or communications
  • Where they would like the Fellowship to take them
  • Their professional goals for the next one to three years
  • One story idea they want to develop
  • One example of previous work

The application is designed to understand the individual applicant rather than simply count previous professional achievements.

The Story Pitch

One of the most important components of the application is the:

One story idea

Applicants should consider:

  • Why the story matters
  • Who is affected
  • Why it matters in Scotland
  • Who they might interview
  • What information they would need
  • What angle makes the story original

The final story must have a clear connection to Scotland or communities living there.

Selection Process

The Fellowship uses a structured selection process.

After the deadline, Migrant Women Press will first carry out:

Eligibility checks

Eligible applications will then be independently assessed.

Each eligible application will be reviewed by:

Two external assessors

using the same assessment framework.

The assessment focuses particularly on:

  • Potential
  • Motivation
  • Curiosity
  • Ideas

rather than simply prior professional privilege or access.

The programme timeline allocates:

14–27 September 2026

for eligibility checks and independent assessment, with applicants informed by 28 September 2026.

Number of Fellowship Places

For the 2026–27 programme, Migrant Women Press plans to select:

Eight Fellows.

Because the cohort is relatively small, applicants should expect the selection process to be competitive.

Can Students Apply?

Yes.

The Fellowship was specifically designed to accommodate:

  • Students
  • Recent graduates
  • Workers
  • People with caring responsibilities

Most training takes place online and in the evening.

However, applicants should be realistic about the programme commitment.

Expected Commitment

Fellows are expected to:

  • Attend and actively participate in training
  • Meet with their mentor approximately once a month
  • Set aside independent time for research
  • Conduct interviews
  • Write their story
  • Fact-check
  • Complete revisions
  • Meet editorial deadlines
  • Participate meaningfully in the industry placement
  • Communicate with MWP when difficulties arise
  • Participate in evaluation
  • Attend the final Glasgow event where possible

Flexibility and Support

Migrant Women Press recognizes that participants may have:

  • Work commitments
  • Study commitments
  • Caring responsibilities
  • Health needs
  • Accessibility needs

The programme aims to provide flexibility and support where challenges arise.

At the same time, applicants are asked to consider carefully whether they can realistically participate between October 2026 and April 2027.

Accessibility and Reasonable Adjustments

The Fellowship emphasizes accessibility.

Applicants who need:

  • Reasonable adjustments
  • Accessibility support
  • Alternative application arrangements

are encouraged to contact Migrant Women Press.

Requesting accessibility support will not disadvantage the application or affect selection.

Information about accessibility requirements will be treated sensitively.

Alternative Application Support

If completing a written application creates a barrier, applicants are encouraged to contact the organisation to discuss:

  • Alternative formats
  • Reasonable adjustments
  • Other support

Contact:

migrantwomenpress@gmail.com

Fellowship Timeline at a Glance

According to the Applicant Guide, the main timeline is:

Date Activity
31 August 2026 Applications open
13 September 2026, 11:59 PM Applications close
14–27 September 2026 Eligibility checks and independent assessment
By 28 September 2026 Applicants informed
Early October 2026 Fellowship begins, induction and mentor matching
October 2026–January 2027 Training, mentoring, reporting and editorial development
January 2027 Online story publication
February 2027 Fellowship print magazine
February–April 2027 Industry placements
April 2027 Final Fellowship event in Glasgow

The Applicant Guide notes that programme dates may be subject to change and Fellows will be updated where necessary.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted using the official online form:

Application form:
https://forms.gle/txTSWKvLXZpDd5Cv5

Before submitting, applicants are strongly encouraged to review:

  • Fellowship Concept Note
  • Applicant Guide and Q&A
  • Fellowship Programme at a Glance

The Applicant Guide specifically recommends checking the full programme commitment before applying.

Application Deadline

Applications close on:

Sunday, 13 September 2026 at 11:59 PM

Late applications should not be assumed to be accepted.

Candidates should allow enough time to:

  • Prepare their story pitch
  • Choose a previous work example
  • Develop thoughtful application responses
  • Request accessibility support if necessary

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

1. Focus on Potential, Not Prestige

The Fellowship explicitly says that selection is based on potential and motivation rather than simply previous access to prestigious journalism opportunities.

Do not assume you need:

  • Major publications
  • National newsroom experience
  • A large portfolio

Instead, demonstrate what you want to learn and why.

2. Develop a Strong Scotland-Connected Story Idea

Your story pitch is important.

A good idea should have:

  • Clear relevance
  • A defined angle
  • Reporting potential
  • Real people or communities to speak with
  • A meaningful Scotland connection

You do not need to have completed the reporting before applying.

3. Explain Why Journalism Matters to You

Avoid writing only that journalism is “interesting.”

Explain what draws you to the field.

Perhaps you want to:

  • Challenge stereotypes
  • Investigate injustice
  • Tell underrepresented stories
  • Improve public understanding
  • Build more inclusive media

Make your motivation specific.

4. Be Honest About Your Career Stage

The programme is designed for emerging journalists.

You do not need to make yourself appear more experienced than you are.

Instead, explain:

  • What you have already done
  • What barriers you have faced
  • What skills you want to develop
  • What you hope to achieve over the next one to three years

5. Choose Your Work Sample Strategically

Your work example does not need to be professionally published.

Choose the piece that best demonstrates:

  • Curiosity
  • Research
  • Storytelling
  • Analysis
  • Writing
  • Communication

rather than simply choosing the work associated with the most prestigious institution.

6. Show That You Understand the Commitment

The Fellowship requires work over several months.

Demonstrating that you understand the training, mentoring, story-production and placement commitments can strengthen your application.

Important Details at a Glance

Organisation: Migrant Women Press

Programme: Emerging Women Journalists Fellowship 2026–27

Number of places: 8

Location requirement: Scotland

Programme duration: October 2026–April 2027

Training: Primarily online

Training period: October 2026–January 2027

Mentoring: One-to-one, normally monthly

Story: Approximately 1,000 words plus at least two interviews and multimedia

Publication: Online and print

Industry placement: Approximately three months, February–April 2027

Placement workload: Normally one or two days per week

Stipend: £600

Travel: Reasonable travel expenses for necessary in-person placements covered

Final event: Glasgow, April 2027

Deadline: 13 September 2026 at 11:59 PM

Application:
https://forms.gle/txTSWKvLXZpDd5Cv5

Questions/accessibility support:
migrantwomenpress@gmail.com

Conclusion

The Migrant Women Press Emerging Women Journalists Fellowship 2026–27 offers eight emerging women journalists from migrant and adversely racialised backgrounds in Scotland an opportunity to strengthen their journalism skills, gain professional media experience and build meaningful industry connections.

Running from October 2026 to April 2027, the Fellowship combines journalism training, monthly one-to-one mentoring, editorial development, publication, networking and a three-month industry placement.

Selected participants receive a £600 stipend, paid in two £300 instalments, in recognition of their participation and the work involved in researching, reporting and producing their Fellowship story.

Fellows will produce an approximately 1,000-word original feature, normally involving at least two interviews and a multimedia component, with support from their mentor and the Migrant Women Press editorial team.

The programme also provides practical industry experience through a part-time placement with a newsroom, media organisation or communications team between February and April 2027.

Applicants should be based in Scotland, come from a migrant and/or adversely racialised background and normally be studying journalism, media, communications or a related subject, or have graduated from a relevant programme within the last three years. Trans women are welcome to apply.

The Fellowship is designed to assess potential, ideas, motivation and curiosity, meaning applicants do not need extensive professional journalism experience or major publication credits.

Applications close on:

Sunday, 13 September 2026 at 11:59 PM.

Successful applicants are expected to be informed by:

28 September 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is inviting qualified professionals to apply for four home-based consultancy opportunities supporting global and regional work in communications, gender-based violence prevention, harmful practices, female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C), research, advocacy and accountability.

The opportunities are designed for professionals with relevant academic qualifications and practical experience who can contribute to UNFPA programmes remotely. The assignments cover areas ranging from internal communications and technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) to research on harmful practices and evidence-based advocacy on FGM/C.

The four opportunities have different requirements, durations and application deadlines, so interested applicants should carefully review the specific Terms of Reference before applying.

UNFPA Home-Based Consultancy Opportunities 2026

The available positions are:

  1. Internal Communications Consultant
  2. Consultant Expert on TFGBV Capacity Strengthening of Frontline Service
  3. Consultant to Document Successful Programming Approaches on Addressing Harmful Practices
  4. Consultant on FGM Evidence-Based Advocacy and Accountability

All four positions are home-based, although the nature of individual assignments and operational requirements may differ.

1. Internal Communications Consultant

The Internal Communications Consultant will support UNFPA’s internal communications and stakeholder engagement activities under the Media and Communications Branch of the Division of External Relations.

The consultant will contribute to the implementation of the UNFPA global communications strategy and produce communications materials for internal audiences.

Key Details
